insider_note: Two components, two signs. Write the sign with each: solute potential is always negative, and pressure potential is positive in a turgid cell.

steps.label: Water potential defined
steps.margin_note: Definition, what it drives, unit, and the zero reference. Six or seven lines.
lines: Water potential (psi w) measures the tendency
of water to move from one part of a plant to
another.
It drives diffusion, osmosis and absorption.
It is measured in pascals (Pa).
Pure water at standard temperature and
pressure has a water potential of ZERO.
steps.why: Pure water is fixed at zero so every real solution can be compared against one agreed starting point; that is what makes water potential a scale and not just a description.
common_mistakes: Giving no unit. Water potential is measured in pascals (Pa).
Saying pure water has the highest positive value. It is set at ZERO, and every solution falls BELOW it.
steps.memory_tip: Pure water is the zero mark on the scale; adding anything to it can only push the value down.

steps.label: Solute potential
steps.margin_note: Name it, say what causes it, and state the sign. The sign is the mark.
lines: Water potential has two components.
1. Solute potential (psi s):
When a solute is dissolved in pure water, the
concentration of free water molecules falls.
So the water potential also falls.
This fall is called solute potential.
It is ALWAYS negative.
steps.why: Dissolving anything reduces the free water available, so the value can only drop — which is why solute potential can never be a positive number.
common_mistakes: Writing solute potential as positive. It is always NEGATIVE.
Confusing it with concentration. It is the FALL in water potential the solute causes.
steps.memory_tip: Solute pulls the value down: add solute, subtract potential.

steps.label: Pressure potential
steps.margin_note: Name it, the cause, the sign, and one place it is seen. Do not skip 'turgid'.
lines: 2. Pressure potential (psi p):
When water enters a plant cell, it presses
against the cell wall.
The cell becomes turgid (swollen).
This rise in water potential is called
pressure potential.
It is usually positive.
In a turgid cell the wall presses back, so the
pressure potential is positive.
steps.why: The wall pushes back on the water inside, and that push adds to the potential — the opposite sign to solute potential, which is why the two are listed as a pair.
common_mistakes: Writing pressure potential as negative inside a turgid cell. Inside a cell it is POSITIVE; in the xylem it turns negative (tension), which is what helps water rise.
Leaving out turgidity. The pressure comes from the swollen cell pushing on its wall.
steps.memory_tip: Pressure pushes the value up; solute pulls it down. Opposite causes, opposite signs.

steps.label: The equation
steps.margin_note: Box the equation and say the two terms are added. Four lines is enough.

lines.text: psi w  =  psi s  +  psi p

lines: Total water potential is the sum of solute
potential and pressure potential.
Because psi s is negative and psi p is
positive, the two work against each other.
steps.why: The equation is the whole answer in one line: it says the two components are added, and the signs already established decide which way each one pulls.
common_mistakes: Writing the two terms as a subtraction. They are ADDED; the minus is already inside psi s.
Leaving the equation out. It is the line the examiner scans for.
steps.memory_tip: One sum, two signs: a negative solute term plus a positive pressure term.
